saints.name: St. Elizabeth of Hungary
saints.title: Religious
saints.shortBlurb: The young princess and widow who spent herself and her wealth on the sick and the poor…
biography: Daughter of King Andrew II of Hungary, Elizabeth was born in 1207 and married Louis IV, Landgrave of Thuringia. A devoted wife and mother, she was known for her ardent charity, building a hospital below the Wartburg and serving the sick and poor with her own hands; the legend of the loaves that turned to roses grew from this love.

Widowed in 1227 when Louis died on crusade, she embraced the poverty of the Third Order of St. Francis, renounced the comforts of the court, and gave herself wholly to the care of the destitute at Marburg. Worn out by penance and service, she died there on 17 November 1231, aged only twenty-four. She is a patroness of the Third Order Franciscans and of charitable works.
saints.knownFor: Her charity to the poor and sick as a widowed Franciscan tertiary.
